scale: Elapsed TAI SI seconds from chosen UTC epoch converted using historical IERS offsets; pre-1961 entries use explicitly approximate UT1-to-TT reconstructions.
approximation: Unknown second: italic approximation sign and finest decimal rounding invariant across the source day/minute window; pre-1961 estimates capped at whole Ms. Documented second-level instants keep six places. Underlying windows retained internally.

events.title: Belka and Strelka return safely to Earth
events.summary: Belka and Strelka return safely after an orbital flight, helping prepare the way for human spaceflight.
events.sourceNotes: NASA StarChild gives August 19 launch and return one day later, August 20, 1960. NASA SP-4012 table (NTRS 19700011921) corroborates reentry 8/20/60. Return day only; do not substitute launch day or infer a landing time. Avoid the source’s overbroad claim about first living creatures returned from space: earlier suborbital flights carried survivors. Checked November 12, 2026.

events.title: Gagarin launches on the first human orbital flight
events.summary: Vostok 1 carries Yuri Gagarin into orbit, opening the era of human spaceflight.
events.sourceNotes: ESA chronology gives April 12, 1961 launch at 06:07 UTC. Retain minute-only precision; no invented :00 seconds. Source rechecked November 12, 2026.

events.title: Cosmic microwave background findings published
events.summary: Penzias and Wilson report background radiation that provides powerful evidence for the Big Bang.
events.sourceNotes: Journal issue date, explicitly identified by the contemporary AIP account; not an observation timestamp.

events.title: Armstrong takes the first step onto the Moon
events.summary: A person steps onto another world. This is the chosen zero point for First Step Epoch.
events.sourceNotes: Chosen FSE convention retained unchanged; not a new determination of the historical instant.

events.title: Gene Cernan completes the final Apollo moonwalk
events.summary: Gene Cernan reenters Apollo 17’s lunar module after the final moonwalk of the Apollo era.
events.sourceNotes: December 14 UTC is the final Apollo 17 EVA/return day. NASA SP-4029 lists 05:40:56 UTC as cabin repressurization, not a second-level timestamp of Cernan’s last footstep; retain day precision for this milestone. NASA’s Remembering Gene Cernan confirms his distinction as last human to leave footprints on the Moon. Treat last-person wording as of the November 2026 review, not a prediction about future missions. Checked November 12, 2026.

events.title: Lucy sheds light on human origins
events.summary: A 3.2-million-year-old skeleton discovered in Ethiopia provides remarkable evidence of how our early relatives walked upright.
events.sourceNotes: ASU Institute of Human Origins dates the discovery by Donald Johanson and Tom Gray at Hadar to November 24, 1974. Smithsonian AL 288-1 anatomy supports upright walking. No clock time supplied. The date is the discovery, not the fossil’s geological age or later publication. Checked November 12, 2026.

events.title: Louise Brown is born following IVF
events.summary: The first birth following in vitro fertilization turns years of reproductive research into a new medical possibility.
events.sourceNotes: Nobel Assembly’s 2010 medicine account confirms Louise Brown’s birth on July 25, 1978. Birth date, not embryo transfer or announcement. No clock time inferred. Rechecked November 12, 2026.

events.title: Smallpox is declared eradicated
events.summary: Vaccination, surveillance, and international cooperation eliminate a devastating human disease.
events.sourceNotes: World Health Assembly declaration date, not the last case or earlier certification.

events.title: Antarctic ozone-hole findings published
events.summary: Long-term measurements reveal severe seasonal ozone loss, helping motivate an international response.
events.sourceNotes: Publication date confirmed by BAS’s fortieth-anniversary account.

events.title: First close-up exploration of Neptune
events.summary: Voyager 2 reaches Neptune, revealing intricate rings, powerful storms, and an unexpectedly active moon, Triton.
events.sourceNotes: NASA mission history documents closest approach August 25, 1989 at 03:56 UT. Retain minute precision without inventing seconds. This timestamp marks the Neptune encounter; the scientific findings describe the wider encounter and subsequent analysis, not simultaneous discoveries. Reviewed November 12, 2026.

events.title: The first confirmed exoplanet system reported
events.summary: Wolszczan and Frail’s pulsar-planet paper establishes that planetary systems exist beyond our own.
events.sourceNotes: Journal publication date; distinguish these pulsar planets from 1995’s first confirmed planet around a Sun-like star.

events.title: Dolly is born
events.summary: The first mammal cloned from an adult cell changes our understanding of cellular development.
events.sourceNotes: Birth date; public announcement followed in 1997.

events.title: The reported exoplanet tally reaches 100
events.summary: A contemporary announcement of Tau¹ Gruis’s planet marks the rapid growth of exoplanet discovery.
events.sourceNotes: PPARC announcement reproduced by ScienceDaily: September 17 within release; republication September 23. Historical reported tally, not a universal catalog ordering.

events.title: Human Genome Project completion announced
events.summary: An international collaboration delivers a foundational human reference sequence, opening new routes into biology and medicine.
events.sourceNotes: Announcement date; essentially complete reference, not gap-free sequencing.

events.title: First comet samples returned to Earth
events.summary: Stardust delivers dust collected from comet Wild 2, bringing material from an ancient Solar System body into laboratories on Earth.
events.sourceNotes: NASA dates Sample Return Capsule return to January 15, 2006. This card uses the return day, not the January 2004 comet encounter or later laboratory findings. Day-only precision; no clock time inferred. Reviewed November 12, 2026.

events.title: Neanderthal genome findings announced
events.summary: Ancient DNA reveals evidence of interbreeding, giving researchers a new way to investigate human history.
events.sourceNotes: Max Planck announcement; journal issue followed May 7. Draft genome, not a gap-free sequence.

events.title: The 1,000-exoplanet catalog milestone reported
events.summary: The Extrasolar Planets Encyclopaedia reaches a thousand worlds, showing how quickly the field has expanded.
events.sourceNotes: IAC report date, not an asserted crossing instant; named catalog because totals differ.

events.title: Gravitational waves directly detected
events.summary: LIGO detects ripples from merging black holes, opening a new way to observe the universe.
events.sourceNotes: Detection at 09:50:45 UTC, at source’s stated precision; announcement February 2016.

events.title: The first black-hole image released
events.summary: A worldwide telescope network resolves bright emission surrounding the shadow of M87’s central black hole.
events.sourceNotes: Release date; observations were collected in 2017.

events.title: First asteroid-deflection demonstration
events.summary: DART impacts Dimorphos, demonstrating a technique for changing an asteroid’s orbit.
events.sourceNotes: NASA DART Final Technical Report records physical impact on September 26, 2022 at 23:14:24 UTC. Not Earth receipt time or the October confirmation announcement. Orbital change established through subsequent observations. Retain documented whole-second precision. Reviewed November 12, 2026.

1965-07-01.title: The Big Bang’s afterglow discovered
1965-07-01.summary: Penzias and Wilson identify the cosmic microwave background, providing powerful evidence that the universe began in a hot, dense state.

1969-07-21T02:56:15Z.title: First step on the Moon
1969-07-21T02:56:15Z.summary: Armstrong steps onto another world, setting FSE’s zero point.

1960-08-20.title: First animals return safely from orbit
1960-08-20.summary: Belka and Strelka return alive from Earth orbit, demonstrating that animals could survive the journey into space and back.

1961-04-12T06:07Z.title: First human in space
1961-04-12T06:07Z.summary: Yuri Gagarin orbits Earth aboard Vostok 1, opening the era of human spaceflight.

1972-12-14.title: Most recent person to walk on the Moon
1972-12-14.summary: Gene Cernan reenters Apollo 17’s lunar module after the final moonwalk of the Apollo era.

1974-11-24.title: Lucy sheds light on human origins
1974-11-24.summary: A 3.2-million-year-old skeleton discovered in Ethiopia provides remarkable evidence of how our early relatives walked upright.

1978-07-25.title: First child born through IVF
1978-07-25.summary: Louise Brown’s birth demonstrates that fertilization outside the body can lead to a successful pregnancy, opening a new chapter in reproductive medicine.

1980-05-08.title: Smallpox declared eradicated
1980-05-08.summary: Vaccination, surveillance, and international cooperation eliminate a devastating human disease, demonstrating what a worldwide scientific effort can achieve.

1985-05-16.title: Antarctic ozone hole findings published
1985-05-16.summary: British Antarctic Survey scientists reveal severe seasonal ozone loss above Antarctica, helping set the stage for international action to protect Earth’s atmosphere.

1989-08-25T03:56Z.title: First close-up exploration of Neptune
1989-08-25T03:56Z.summary: Voyager 2 reaches Neptune, revealing intricate rings, powerful storms, and an unexpectedly active moon, Triton.

1992-01-09.title: First planets confirmed beyond our Solar System
1992-01-09.summary: Aleksander Wolszczan and Dale Frail report planets orbiting a pulsar, establishing that our Solar System is not the only planetary system.

1996-07-05.title: First mammal cloned from an adult cell
1996-07-05.summary: Dolly’s birth demonstrates that the genetic material in a specialized adult cell can support the development of a whole animal, changing our understanding of cellular development.

2002-09-17.title: Exoplanet discoveries reach 100
2002-09-17.summary: Astronomers announce a planet orbiting Tau¹ Gruis, bringing the reported tally to 100 and revealing a growing diversity of planetary systems.

2003-04-14.title: Human Genome Project completed
2003-04-14.summary: An international collaboration completes a landmark human reference sequence, opening new ways to investigate biology, disease, and our shared ancestry.

2006-01-15.title: First comet samples returned to Earth
2006-01-15.summary: Stardust delivers dust collected from comet Wild 2, bringing material from an ancient Solar System body into laboratories on Earth.

2013-10-23.title: Exoplanet catalog reaches 1,000 worlds
2013-10-23.summary: The Extrasolar Planets Encyclopaedia lists a thousand worlds, showing how rapidly exploration beyond our Solar System has expanded.

2015-09-14T09:50:45Z.title: First direct detection of gravitational waves
2015-09-14T09:50:45Z.summary: LIGO detects ripples from merging black holes, opening a new way to observe the universe.

2022-09-26T23:14:24Z.title: First asteroid-deflection demonstration
2022-09-26T23:14:24Z.summary: DART impacts Dimorphos, demonstrating a technique for changing an asteroid’s orbit.

2010-05-06.title: Ancient DNA reveals our Neanderthal connections
2010-05-06.summary: Researchers reconstruct a draft Neanderthal genome, revealing evidence of interbreeding with modern humans and opening a new way to explore our shared past.

2019-04-10.title: First image of a black hole released
2019-04-10.summary: A worldwide network of radio telescopes reveals the shadow of the black hole in galaxy M87, turning an extraordinary prediction into an observable image.
